rating.reasoning_summary: This strand centers on @exgenesis's "Big Picture" diagram—a hierarchical map tracing information flow from individual experience to global coordination and human flourishing. The boundary object is the Scapple diagram itself, which evolves from a raw whiteboard sketch (2022) to a polished visual artifact that becomes a reference point for the post-rationalist community. The arc is constructive rather than dialectical: exgenesis creates the map, shares iterations, receives encouragement and requests for clarification, and the artifact becomes a 'quest map' for the scene. The strand lacks conflict or refinement through debate—it's primarily appreciation and citation. While the diagram is intellectually ambitious (spanning meditation to AI alignment), the Twitter discourse around it remains shallow: people say 'this is cool' but don't engage with specific nodes or challenge the structure. The podcast episode with Tasshin provides the only deep dive. The map has high symbolic utility (it's a 'flag' for the community's aspirations) but unclear practical utility—no one reports using it to guide action.

title: The “Quest Map of Postrat Twitter” goes viral
summary:
The most quotable moment is @0xAshith looking at @exgenesis’s sprawling “Big Picture” diagram and just dubbing it: “Questmap of postrat twitter.” That basically became the community’s whole relationship to it: a single image that tries to route “epistemic bedrock (experience)” all the way up to “global coordination” and “human flourishing in deep time,” with nodes like meditation/phenomenology → bottom‑up sensemaking → collective sensemaking → multi‑scale organizing → digital democracy/AI alignment/etc. Exgenesis explicitly frames it as “a map of things you can focus on if you want to help,” while people like @QiaochuYuan praise the specific throughline of “individual sensemaking practices feeding into collective sensemaking.”

The arc is basically: raw whiteboard brain-dump (Aug 12, 2022) → everyone begging for a readable version. @loopholekid pushes the “hire a part-time research assistant to digitize this” angle; @visakanv straight-up requests a @scappleapp version “so it’s easy to read,” which exgenesis delivers, and that cleaned-up v2 (Aug 23) is the artifact that spreads. The peak is mostly admiration + recruitment: @lemondotpng calls it “coherent genius-level,” and @burny_tech uses the QRI Discord as the “let’s make this real collectively” coordination funnel (with @lemondotpng vouching hard for the Discord’s vibe). The closest thing to conflict is @kanzure sniping “too much woo, not enough technological self-actualization,” and then… it doesn’t really turn into a fight; exgenesis just goes “let’s hear it!” and the thread moves on.

Then the vibe quietly shifts from “this is a roadmap” to “this is beautiful but unreadable”: a week later exgenesis jokes that their best contributions are “too illegible” to monetize, pointing right back to the diagram as exhibit A. The only real deep engagement comes later when @tasshinfogleman does a full podcast episode unpacking it (Apr 2023), and the map periodically resurfaces as a totem—most notably in 2025 when exgenesis reposts it because Tasshin says “this is important for the world.” Why care: it’s a perfect case study in how online scenes turn one dense diagram into a shared identity + coordination fantasy… and how rarely anyone does the boring work of turning the “quest map” into actual quests.
